Participants said the labor market remained strong, with the unemployment rate at a 50-year low and solid job gains continuing. [2020-01-29/participantsViews/6] They noted that payroll employment was expected to expand at a healthy pace, despite an anticipated reduction in recent payroll growth estimates. [2019-12-11/participantsViews/7] Participants also observed that labor force participation was increasing and expected the unemployment rate to remain low going forward.

Participants noted that overall inflation had continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent objective, especially for items other than food and energy. They observed moderate wage pressures despite this. Market-based measures of inflation compensation and some survey measures of consumer inflation expectations remained low, though they had been gradually improving. Inflation expectations, as reflected in longer-term market data, had declined and stood at historically low levels, with the longer-term market inflation expectations at 1.71% as of September 30, 2019. [2019-07-31/participantsViews/16]

Participants described the housing market as bleak, with falling prices, slow sales, high unsold home inventories, and declining construction activity. At the June 25, 2008 meeting, most participants saw little sign of a bottoming out, though a few noted tentative signs of stabilization in some areas. The market had continued to weaken since the prior meeting, with housing starts and demand for new homes declining further and prices falling faster than in late 2007. [2008-06-25/participantsViews/5] This view was consistent with earlier assessments at the April 30 and March 18 meetings, where participants emphasized deepening contraction and uncertainty about recovery.

Participants noted that consumer spending surged in March and expected further gains would significantly contribute to the economic recovery. They highlighted fiscal stimulus, accommodative financial conditions, and the release of pent-up demand as key drivers. In discussions, participants observed that while spending on services requiring close personal contact remained weak, overall household spending was rising and was seen as essential for broader economic recovery. [2021-04-28/participantsViews/3]

Participants noted that financial market conditions remained under considerable stress, even as some improvements were observed. In June 2008, they acknowledged that liquidity facilities introduced by the Federal Reserve had helped bolster confidence. By October 2008, adverse developments—including Lehman Brothers’ bankruptcy the day before the meeting—had significantly impacted markets, causing a major money market mutual fund’s net asset value to fall below $1. These events highlighted ongoing financial instability and market stress. [2008-06-25/participantsViews/3], [2008-10-29/financialMarkets/9]

Earlier runs since 1990 show that in 3 of 5 cases, mortgage rates increased by a median of +0.2 percentage points after a rate hike.
